sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG handoff hints — Distractions and driving challenges

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
Aggressive operation that endangers others differs from road rage, which additionally requires a criminal act done from a vehicle to menace someone in another vehicle after a roadway incident [A01]
Why it matters: group_hint threat-behavior; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R02]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A02
If confused between staying in lane for an animal and swerving, the handbook rule is to keep control in the travel lane and not swerve, because swerving raises personal-injury risk [A02]
Why it matters: group_hint animal-avoidance; prereq_hint lane-control; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with [sec11-R08]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A03
A mid-trip drowsy stop with a short nap differs from trip planning, which calls for nightly rest, a break about every two hours, a companion observer, and checking medicines for sleepiness [A03]
Why it matters: group_hint fatigue-management; prereq_hint distraction-basics; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with [sec11-R07]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A04
Drivers at least eighteen may talk hands-free with voice commands plus GPS and hazard reporting, while drivers under eighteen may use a device only for medical, hazard, crime, or parent contact needs [A04]
Why it matters: group_hint device-law; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R05]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A04
A texting violation punished as the lower misdemeanor with a capped fine differs from the higher misdemeanor applied when bodily injury results or a prior offense exists [A04]
Why it matters: group_hint device-penalty; prereq_hint sec11-R04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with [sec11-R04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A05
Shallow water reaching a car floor that causes loss of control differs from deeper moving water that can sweep away most vehicles including large trucks, and in both cases the rule is to turn around rather than cross [A05]
Why it matters: group_hint flood-response; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R11]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A05
Orange work-zone signs with at least doubled speeding fines differ from ordinary signs, and drivers must slow even with no workers present, widen following space, and continue until the end-of-work notice [A05]
Why it matters: group_hint work-zone; prereq_hint sign-color; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R03]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A07
Steering toward the skid side differs from braking hard, so ease off the accelerator, steer gently the same way the rear slides, avoid oversteer and hard braking, then straighten once grip returns [A07]
Why it matters: group_hint skid-recovery; prereq_hint speed-control; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R02]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A06
Yielding to uphill traffic on a narrow descent differs from coasting in neutral, which is prohibited, and drivers should use a low gear, keep right, and sound the horn at blind sharp curves [A06]
Why it matters: group_hint mountain-driving; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R12]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A08
A vehicle that floats only briefly after entering water calls for belt removal and window exit to the roof, while a fast-sinking vehicle with stuck exits calls for waiting for pressure balance, shedding heavy clothes, and using the air pocket [A08]
Why it matters: group_hint submersion-escape; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with [sec11-R06]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A09
Letting hot-tire pressure stay high differs from bleeding it off, and drivers should also watch coolant gauges, expect slippery tar bleed, and use low beams in fog or snow [A09]
Why it matters: group_hint weather-vehicle; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R06]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A06
Dimming for oncoming traffic at the longer distance differs from dimming when following at the shorter distance, and limited visibility also requires lights on and longer following space without tinted lenses at night [A06]
Why it matters: group_hint night-driving; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with [sec11-R09]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0070]
